headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, RSI stretched into the 70s, and whale wallets still trending onto exchanges for a third straight week
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, MACD confirms above signal on every one of them, and only DOGE and ADA sit below trend with DOGE's MACD still bullish against a broken 200-day, a small crack in an otherwise unified picture. That's six of seven majors in a confirmed uptrend structurally, which is a different market than the mixed, one-off-here-one-off-there tape this desk usually has to describe.

But trend and momentum are starting to argue with each other. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 71.3, ETH at 70.5, SOL at 75.2: all three in classic overbought territory, and SOL in particular is up 23.2% on the week and 40.1% on the month while still 57.6% below its 12-month high. That combination, strong trend plus stretched momentum plus a long way from the old high, says this is a real rally that has moved fast, not a market gently drifting upward. ADA is the outlier the other direction: MACD below signal, below its 200-day, RSI a neutral 52.7, down 0.9% on the day even as it's still up 7.6% on the week and 20.7% on the month. Worth naming since the daily and weekly windows disagree there, same as DOGE.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0014% per 8 hours (1.6% annualized), cheap by any standard, with a long/short ratio of 1.25 and open interest at $2.22B. ETH's funding is similarly tame at 1.1% annualized. But SOL funding is negative, -0.0099% per 8h (-10.8% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to stay in the trade, and yet SOL's long/short ratio is 1.68, more longs than shorts by account count. That's a genuine divergence: negative funding usually says the crowd is leaning short, but the account ratio says otherwise, and 24h liquidations of $537K in shorts versus $280K in longs on SOL suggest the shorts have been the ones getting hurt. XRP's long/short ratio of 2.46 and DOGE's 3.96 show a much more lopsided long crowd on the smaller names, which is the kind of crowded, one-sided setup this desk calls fragile rather than fuel.

Now the flows, and here's the real tension of the day. BTC ETFs printed a net outflow of $201.9M on 28 Aug, but the five-session net is a positive $924.5M, and same_direction_days of just 1 tells you that single-day outflow broke a run rather than confirming one. ETH ETFs are more consistent: $102.1M in on the day, $815.7M over five sessions, ten straight same-direction days, an actual accumulating bid. Meanwhile whale wallets moved a net $18.0M off exchanges in the last 24 hours, a mild reduction in available supply, but zoom out to the weekly data and the story flips: three straight weeks of net flow onto exchanges, $508M (week ending Aug 15), $1,062M (week ending Aug 22), and $659M (week ending Aug 29). A single day of coins leaving exchanges sitting inside three weeks of coins arriving is not a contradiction to wave away, it's the tape telling you the multi-week supply trend and the most recent day don't agree yet.

Sentiment, for what it's worth, is Greed at 68, sitting near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74. That lines up with the price action and the stretched RSI readings, crowd mood and momentum are both running hot together, which is more confirmation than divergence this time. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.11% over 30 days to $309.8B, not the kind of dry-powder surge that usually accompanies euphoric tops.

What to watch: whether BTC's five-session ETF flow stays positive after a day like this one, whether the weekly whale exchange-flow series prints a fourth straight week onto exchanges or finally reverses, and whether SOL's negative funding alongside its long-heavy account ratio resolves through a funding flip or a liquidation flush. Any one of those changing would be the first real crack in an otherwise cleanly aligned uptrend.
